utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. MIRA TADIC, recalled. Examined by MR. KAY, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Tadic, you understand that you are still under the oath that you took yesterday to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Tadic, as we concluded the evidence yesterday afternoon you were telling the Court about your husband's job involving carpentry work at Sisak in Croatia. You had also told us about your own work that in the late 1980s was, in fact, at the hospital in Prijedor -- in Kozarac, not the hospital in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did Dusko Tadic work in this company with the carpentry business in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the year that that business ended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Summer 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time were you still living in the ground floor of the house in Kalate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you continue to live in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that house, well, we lived there until my father-in-law died in 1989. Then we went back to the family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you went back to the family house, was your husband still working in Croatia or had his business finished there and had he returned back to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When your father-in-law died -- that is Ostoja Tadic, is it not ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- did you then move into part of the house of the Tadic family with your children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it the same part of the house that you had lived in before or was it a different part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a different part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we just look at that photograph we looked at yesterday afternoon? If Exhibit 300 could be put in front of the witness? (Handed) If you actually put it on the monitor and then she can indicate where.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were living in that part in the middle. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could leave the photograph there, is that the part of the house that you continued to live in or did eventually you move to another part of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the month of August 1991 we moved to the upper part -- the loft actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could just keep your indicator for a moment on the photograph a little bit longer so that we can see it? That is the floor above the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Having had the carpentry business in Croatia, what was Dusko Tadic's next employment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afterwards we were building our own premises and on and off he would go and join his brother who was working in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What work would he do in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His brother had a construction company and that is where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which brother is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which town in Germany was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Munchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have referred to another part of the house where eventually you went to live. Did there come a time when Dusko Tadic opened up a cafe in part of the family home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the extension to the family house. Am I supposed to indicate it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you could, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you just indicate there? If you could keep it on so that we can see it for a moment longer? That part of the house there on the right-hand side which has a square front, was that built later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That entire part I am indicating now was all added as an extension -- that is the part that we built -- and the part down here was the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the name of the cafe the Nipon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did that building work start for the extension to the family home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1989, spring 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when that work started was your father-in-law still alive at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but then in the meantime he passed away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was the work on that part of the house completed so that you were able to move into that side of the family home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do apologise. I have not quite understood. Are you referring to the business premises or the upper storey?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, the upper storey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the upper storey, well, we have moved into it in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was the cafe bar opened which is on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prior to that, before we moved into the upper storey, by the end of 1990, beginning of 1991, that is when we opened the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it right that other people within the town of Kozarac helped at times in doing some of the building work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that on a regular basis that people would help on the building work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, whenever there was major construction work to be done, but no skilled, highly skilled, workers were required.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How was the building of this part of the house paid for? How was it financed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A part of that was borne by my husband, another part by his brother and we also loaned some money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did people also give their services and help for free, for no reward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that something that was a tradition or something that was expected in that community of Kozarac, if people were undertaking this kind of work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time were you still working in the hospital in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that as a general nurse or did you have any particular skill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A general nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you about relationships between Dusko Tadic and other people within the town of Kozarac by this time in 1990. Did you have many friends in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were those friends of all different ethnic groups, Serbian, Croat and Muslim friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had lived with Dusko Tadic for over 10 years by this time. In that 10 years did he have particularly close friends from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one of his childhood friends was Ahmed Kulenovic and he remained friends with him, then Fikret Sakanovic, Emir Karabasic, Hamdo Balic later on, Sefika Arnautovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned there Emir Karabasic; had he been a long standing friend of your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at a photograph. There is a colour picture here for you to see and tell me, first of all, if you recognise this photograph which I tender to the Court as D71.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph, Mrs. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think sometime in 1985 or 1986 while on summer holiday in Pula.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are copies here for your Honours and perhaps if that could be put on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection to Defence Exhibit 71. It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. It is a small photograph, so if we could have it blown up into as full a size as possible? Can you move it down the monitor a little bit? That is fine. Mrs. Tadic, I would like you to turn to the right and with that pointer if you could indicate who are the people within that photograph that you recognise. Keep the pointer for a few seconds upon each person as you identify them so that we can take in exactly to whom you are indicating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Stojan Tadic, the eldest of my husband's brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my eldest daughter, Valentina Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the one sitting here is Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If that photograph can be moved down a little bit more so that we can see the gentleman in the right-hand corner a little bit better? Thank you. Standing on the right-hand side on the brickwork there, who is that? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. This is not my husband, if you mean him. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Yes, I thought it was but I am obviously wrong about that. OK. Thank you. So there is a holiday photograph in 1985 or 1986 with Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It must have been 1984, 1985, judging by my daughter's age. She must have been four or five in that picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you think your husband took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So he was on holiday with you and was Karabasic and Stojan Tadic also on holiday with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How close was the friendship between your husband and Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand. Do you mean when, in what period of time or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us just take it at this time in the mid 1980s?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then later on in the 1980s, did they remain close friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not after 1991 and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Until 1991 had they always been close friends or had their friendship drifted apart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were always good friends up until 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they remain friends after 1991 or did there come a change in their relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were still friends but they saw each other less frequently. They did not see each other all the time as they used to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was Karabasic a married man like your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On and off, occasionally he was and at other times he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have heard evidence in this Court about your husband's qualifications as a karate teacher and that he used to instruct local school children and others in the sport of karate. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he have a karate school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us when he started the karate school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in 1980 or -- yes, in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did that school continue in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It continued until he left to Libya, 1986. In 1986 Karabasic took over as his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When he returned from Libya, did he continue with the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, then he was tied up with other work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he ever restart the school in Kozarac after he left it in 1986?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he take part in karate sporting competitions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they just local competitions or did he perform elsewhere in Yugoslavia in more national competitions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember we went to one of the State competitions but only once. That is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he perform his sport of karate in competitions outside Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it right that two of his other brothers were also involved in this sport, the elder brother Mladen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And also the other brother Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the three of them ever have any arrangements for teaching this sport which involved the three of them together, or did they have this interest separately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Mladen had his own club in Munchen, Ljubo in Banja Luka and Dule in Kozarac and occasionally, of course, he went to Banja Luka for training from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the good relations that you have talked about between your husband and the people within Kozarac always continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your husband always remain on good terms with the people in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1990 we are aware in this Court of elections that for the first time were to take place in the former Yugoslavia. Did you ever join a political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the party of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you ever been a member of a political party before you joined the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which party was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the League of Communists party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you start your membership of the League of Communists party and for how long did it continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I became a member of the League of Communists in the 4th grade of my nursing school, school for nurses. That was in 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did your membership continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up until 1991, roughly speaking, up until I became a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had your husband Dusko Tadic been politically active in those years that you knew him from when you first met him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he also join the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for the two of you then joining that political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason why we joined that political party were the threatening letters we were receiving in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many letters did you receive of a threatening nature in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did that letter say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That letter had a very -- was threatening, saying that we should leave Kozarac and if we do not leave Kozarac within three months that we would be killed, and it was signed by the "Young Muslims from Kozarac", that is the party of SDA -- the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the time that you received that letter were you then not a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I became a member later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does that also go for your husband Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We also know from evidence in this Court about a plebiscite that was held in November 1991 and I would like you to see Prosecution Exhibit 146. Perhaps the English translation could be put on the monitor to assist the Court and the witness look at the original in Serbo-Croat? (Handed) Thank you. It is all right. You have no need to use the indicator; it is just for information purposes. You look at that document we have put in front of you. This is a document dated 8th November 1991 which is in the bottom left-hand corner and slightly off the screen. Do you see that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the top of this document it reads that it is an instruction for the plebiscite of Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina to be held on 9th and 10th November 1991. There is a decision appointing voting officials for the plebiscite in the area of Kozarac and Vidovici. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see beneath there a list of names. At point (1), for President, your husband is named as Dusko Tadic with a deputy. At point (2) there are other names. Then at point (3) we see for member, Bosa Majkic, and for deputy, Mirjana Tadic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have been called Mira Tadic, but is that, in fact, your full name, Mirjana Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. This is a mistake. My real name is just Mira, but it does speak about me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is you, though?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could tell us about this, first of all, from your husband's position. How did he become involved in this plebiscite of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to tell you like this, in 1991 the Serbian people wanted to remain in Yugoslavia, and in the area of Kozarac there were only around 10 per cent of Serbian households and somebody had to organise them. So, we took it upon us to organise this plebiscite, that is, that the Serbian people should express themselves and state whether they want to remain in Yugoslavia and keep this right to live in the country in which -- the state where they have lived up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By this time in November 1991 were both you and your husband already members of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To become a member of the SDS at that time what did you have to do? How did you become a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We simply went to the hospital and became members. That is the only thing we had to do -- simply express the wish to become members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have to fill in a form and was that form sent to the political headquarters of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. We simply received membership cards. Whether we needed something to fill in or not, I cannot remember but I remember that we received the cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To receive those membership cards had you spoken to anyone in particular and said, "I would like to join this particular political party"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that needed to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember to whom you spoke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. We went together to the hospital and there was Bogoljub Glusac. He was there as a Legal Officer in the hospital in Prijedor and we talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you had any political documents or books concerning the philosophy of the SDS and what its political standpoint was for policies on various matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not have anything. Probably there is the Statute of the Party, but we did not have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Once you had joined as members, were you or your husband sent any political books indicating the policies of this political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you or your husband read political books?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as far as I can remember, the Party did not have any books, maybe there was the Statute, but we did not read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you read other books on politics, political science?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read the Islamic declaration by Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am now talking about 1991 and this time of the plebiscite, and the time that you had joined the political party, the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I did not read any political books.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did it come about then that your husband was appointed a voting official in the area of Kozarac and Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that happened because Dule had most free time. Only he and I could organise that. We were young. All the others came from village households and they had more tasks to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So who asked you and he to organise the plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The President of the Party, I think, Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was he based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he come from Kozarac originally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he have any connection with Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You think with Kozarac or with our family?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Either, if you can help us with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether he had any connections with Kozarac, but he was otherwise -- he was linked to our family. He was the -- he was a witness at my -- at a wedding of my brother-in-law Stojan Tadic, best man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the plebiscite held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the courtyard of the church, at the church office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it take place over those two days of 9th and 10th November?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What actually happened on those days of 9th and 10th November?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 9th and 10th November the plebiscite was held. That is, every person that wanted to express feelings to remain within Yugoslavia, they could go to the plebiscite and vote, no matter what nationality they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did many people vote in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Mostly people of Serbian nationality went to vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember how many people turned up to vote over 9th and 10th November?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember how many people, maybe 70 to 100, not more than that. That is more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were those people Serbs who lived in Kozarac or Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were Serbs, I think. A couple of Muslims turned up as well and some Ukrainians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time then at the end of 1991 how were relations within the community of Kozarac between the various ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for that tension?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason for the tension was because the Serbs wanted to remain in Yugoslavia the way that Yugoslavia was. At that time the Muslims wanted their state, Bosnia, and the Croats also wanted a state of their own. That was the reason, and everybody was turning and following their leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have referred to the SDS and you and your husband. Was there actually a party headquarters or office established for the SDS in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Kozarac. The headquarters were in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That then is why you had to go to Prijedor with your husband to meet someone to say you wanted to join the Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any other political parties that were active in Kozarac at this time in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Kozarac the other party that was active was the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How were they active in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they held meetings in Kozarac. People would become members of the Party. Their ideology was spread.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did this affect you as Serbs living in Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, as all of them went into their Party and their -- turned towards their people, suddenly all the people became very politicized. So the effect upon us was that we turned towards our Party and our people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us about the threatening letter that your husband received. Had there been any other problems that you experienced directed against you or your husband or where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was not only this letter of a threatening nature. After that letter, there were phone calls. There were also pressures expressed at your workplace. You could not behave freely. You had to watch out what you were saying. You should not take part into any political discussions. Everything was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time you were still working in the hospital in Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did your husband's cafe open for business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In early '91.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the business like? Was it good or poor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, medium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of people went to that cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In what nationality?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All nationalities, some Serbs, mostly Muslims, some Croats. It depended, but that was the population structure in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your husband was the proprietor of the cafe. Did he have any people who worked there as waiters and helped out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What nationalities were they who worked with him in the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you name any of the Muslim people who had worked there for him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me remember. There was a young man called Suad and before that Sead from Kalate worked there. Then the son of Adil Jakupovic, Braco Jakupovic -- many worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your husband's cafe ever become a place where only Serbs were welcome?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could his cafe have survived if he only restricted it to people from one ethnic background, just Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any acts taken by people against the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, the rumours stating that Muslims could not enter the premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did some Muslims stay away from the premises as a form of boycott?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, mostly the Muslims from the centre of Kozarac boycotted the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason for it was that there was a Serb who held the cafe, who owned the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the other cafes in Kozarac owned by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any damage that was committed against the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On two occasions the shop window was broken and at one time the cafe was broken in and burgled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did your husband Dusko react to these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He reacted in a way because he wanted to stay there till the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he himself commit any acts against other people as some sort of revenge within the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we enter 1992 and some five months before the conflict in Kozarac, what was the state of relations like in the town amongst the different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The relations were tense. Apparently, we would say "hello" and talk, but there were no close contacts or visits. Everybody was just minding their own business.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was causing this tension?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because people were simply afraid of one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you or your husband adding to this tension? Were you or your husband adding to this climate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could not add to it because we were a minority. We were more or less the only ones there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the wishes of both of you that you could live there in the family home and run your business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the wishes of both of you that your children could be brought up in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did people begin to leave Kozarac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of people began to leave? Were they only of one nationality or were they of various ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the people of Muslim nationality started to leave, that is, women were taking the children out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know where these people were going to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly they were going to their relatives in Zagreb, in Germany, wherever they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did all the Serbs remain in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did there come a time when they started to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I left first. I left the first with my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you leave Kozarac first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 1st April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did you leave on 1st April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because at that time in Kozarac it was not safe any more. We were in a minority. The Muslim people became organised. They had their barracks, they wore uniforms, held arms. I was afraid because for my life and for the life of my children, and that is why I left Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 1st April 1992 were you working until that date in the hospital in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever go back to working at the hospital in Kozarac after that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 1st April 1992, then, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I went to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did you go to stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For four days I was staying with my brother-in-law in Banja Luka, Ljubomir Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After that four days where did you go to next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I went to a village near Sanski Most, Kozice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was your connection with that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A friend of mine comes from that village and she invited us to come and stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you stay there? When did you finish living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 29th April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you went to live there, did you take your children with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took my children and my mother-in-law came along as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic go with you and live away from Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he took us there. He drove us and then he went back home on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were taken by him, was that to Ljubo's house or to Kozice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you get to Ljubo's house in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljubo drove us from Kozice to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Ljubomir Tadic have a car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a utility vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a zastava, white coloured, what we call a "combi".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When Dusko Tadic took you to Kozice and, you told us, drove you there, what vehicle did he drive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came along -- no, Ljubo drove us and Dule came along. He was not driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your husband own a car at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has your husband ever owned a car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was between 1981 and 1985. That is when we did have a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you returned from Libya, did he ever own a car then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having stayed in Kozice for nearly a month, where did you go after you left that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we came to the family house in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did you only stay there for that short period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the fourth day we were forced to flee Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened then on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day when we fled Kozarac or on the day before, what was the reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, on the day that you fled Kozarac, what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day there was general chaos in Kozarac. Everybody was in uniform or in shelters, women and children, and we were not invited to go to the shelters and so we wanted to leave Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you leave Kozarac on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day we left together with our priest, Mladen Majkic, in his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mladen Majkic, did he have a family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did his family consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His wife, Veselka Majkic and his daughter, Mladena Majkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you made any arrangement with the priest, Mladen Majkic, that you would leave Kozarac on that day prior to the event happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not really agree on anything. We were not expecting anything like that. That is what happened and we got ready hurriedly and then we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon -- you mean when we left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date? Yes, it was on 3rd May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you left in the car of the priest, who travelled in that car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The priest and his family, in other words, his daughter and his wife, I myself and my husband and my two children and my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it easy for all of you to fit in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could hardly fit in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why was the priest, Mladen Majkic, leaving Kozarac on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because on the day before his wife was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they live in a house in the grounds of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No translation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not get a translation of the last answer. Madam, could you come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Tadic, would you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the house was on the grounds of the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. You had been in Kozarac for only some four days at that time. Do you know if other Serb families had left Kozarac in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During those four days at the beginning of May 1992 did your husband, Dusko Tadic, remain with you in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do apologise I have not understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For those four days that you returned to Kozarac before you left with the priest, Mladen Majkic, had your husband remained also in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it possible for you to drive on the main road when you left Kozarac at this time in early May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not drive along the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us then what happened, what route you took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we left down the main road we were stopped by Sead Bahonjic with an automatic rifle when we arrived at the junction, and he told us we were not allowed to leave Kozarac. Then we said we were going to go to the police station and we were going to ask for authorisation to leave, but we did not stop there. We drove across Kozara and we arrived at the last checkpoint and Mr. Salkanovic was there with a rifle and a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Madam, could you speak more slowly because we have to listen to this and it is difficult to take it all in. I would like you to go back to the beginning again just so that we can get it more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you take it from the point when you described someone as stopping you with a rifle, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Sead Bahonjic in a camouflage uniform wearing glasses and an automatic rifle stopped us and told us we were not allowed to leave Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts was this that he stopped you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you leave the churchyard in the Omladinska Street, you turn right on the road to Banja Luka or Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did he stop you there at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said we were not allowed to leave. I do not know why he stopped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that you said that you would return to the police station to obtain authorisation. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We only told him we were going to the police station. But we did not stop there, but we continued on the road to Makrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So did you drive out of Kozarac on a different road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did that road take you through Mrakovica in the direction of Mount Kozara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we just look at that plan of that map D13 here so that we can get that in mind? If a copy could be put in front of the witness and a copy -- yes, put a copy actually on the overhead monitor so the witness may indicate to us. (Handed). Madam, that is the map that you looked at yesterday, you may recollect. If you could just take a moment to familiarise yourself with it because I am going to ask you to point to where you went on 3rd May in a moment. Can you see Kozarac marked in the middle of the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see that, the triangle that is at the bottom of Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see where the Mutnik Mosque is indicated, if you progress up Marsala Tita Street towards Rajkovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I do not know where the mosque is. Where is the sign for the mosque?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is a round circle beside the road, beside that yellow road beneath the "K" of Mutnik. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do see the circle, if that is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is what it is. Perhaps if that could now be put on the monitor? You indicate with that pointer, if you are able to, where it was that you were first of all stopped by the man with the rifle. That is right. We have the triangle there in the middle of the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right. Can you tell us where the man ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where the junction is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where he was. We were supposed to turn and go down this road and he was standing there and then we went down this road to the hospital, then through this street to the main street and then all straight ahead to Mutnik, and the last checkpoint was here in Rajkovici. There was another man and the first one was standing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that OK?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. That is very clear. Was that man at the first place where you stopped at a checkpoint or was he just standing there on his own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is where the barricades were in the yard of Stoja Coprka. There is a bunker. There were a few people in there, more than one, but he was the one who stopped us but there was a whole group of them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you turned around and went back through Kozarac towards Rajkovici, were you stopped there at another checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last barricades, they attempted to stop us but we did not stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you passed through the barricade there and then where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no further barricades from Rajkovici, and all the way down to Banja Luka, we followed down that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived in Banja Luka on this day, 3rd May 1992, whereabouts did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to my brother-in-law's, Ljubomir Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you remain with the priest, Mladen Majkic, and his family at Ljubomir Tadic's or did he go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He stayed with us that night and then on the day after he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you stay at Ljubo Tadic's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed at Ljubo Tadic's about three to four days, until we found our own accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your husband Dusko remain with you at Ljubo's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until Thursday, until we found another accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at another photograph and it is D62A. (Handed). Can you tell us if you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is it of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the house where we were staying, but we were on the other side, on the ground floor. That is the house where we were in the Koste Jarica Street in Starcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to staying on the other side. Could you look at D62B now? (Handed). Mr. Usher, if you could put both photographs on the monitor after the witness has identified them. D62B, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is that part of the house where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could put both photographs on the monitor now, Mr. Usher? You said that that house was in Koste Jarica Street. Did you know who owned that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know the owner. All I know is that there was a Croat woman whose husband was Ukrainian and in November, the previous year, she had left for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So was anyone living in that house when you went to stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The place where you had been staying the previous four days with Ljubo Tadic, was that a house or a flat, an apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a flat. It was Ljubo's flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many bedrooms were in that flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No bedrooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it a large flat or a small flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he have his family living with him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would there have been room for your family and Ljubo's family to have remained together in that flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you come then to move into the house in Koste Jarica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we just could not all stay in such a small one room flat, and then a friend of Ljubo's found us this other accommodation which he was keeping an eye on, as it were, and so we went to see him and we decided to get that, that we would stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that the part of the house that you lived in was around the other side. Did you live in the whole of this house, which we can see has ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that house was not habitable, just one room was really habitable. Am I to show it on the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the only room that was habitable. This was the hall and the living room. It was all one part, and there was one regular room on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a completely built house? Had it been finished in its state of building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it was not finished. Only one room, as I said, was completely finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it have electricity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it have water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the walls plastered and decorated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the conditions like within this part of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that part of the house there were good conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The rest of the house, the other three storeys that we can see from the front of the house in the photograph on the left, what was their condition like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not a finished house. There was nothing. It was not plastered or -- I just think there was electricity, there were cables in all these other parts on the first and the second floor and the loft.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This part of the house round the back, was that the basement to the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the basement. On this side you cannot see it. You can see it on the other side. That is the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was the friend of Ljubo's who allowed you to stay there who had been keeping an eye on the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a friend -- the brother of a friend of Ljubo's, Nihad Alic and his name was Nedim Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you meet Nedim Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we knew them. For a long time before that we had known them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the arrangement about this house in Banja Luka that you could stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they had given us the house so we could stay there and protect the house as well, because he had the keys to the house and as it was not lived in there were quite a few burglaries. It was broken into several times, and so basically it was convenient to both of us because we were staying at the house and so it was mutually profitable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he indicate that the owner of the house might want to return and live in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What would have happened if that owner had returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nothing would have happened. We would have moved out and she would have been free to move in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that you left Kozarac with your children, your mother-in-law, Dusko Tadic. Were you all living together in the basement of that house from that fourth day in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we stayed. I myself, my mother-in-law and the two daughters and Dule went back to our family house in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, can you clarify this? Do you call this portion in 63B the basement part of the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Is it the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at the first photograph 62A and seeing the three storeys there, this is actually a submerged portion ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: I see, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- at the rear. If you go on the right-hand side, you walk down a steep slope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that right, Mrs. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to clarify your last answer, please. Did you all remain living in that basement of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we moved into the basement of that house, I myself, my mother-in-law and my two children, once we have cleaned it up and we could move in, once that was done, Dule went back to Kozarac, to our family house, and we for security reasons stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long was Dule Tadic then living at that house with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not understood this. What period of time do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, we are dealing with the time that you move into the house and, as you told us, that it had to be cleaned and then he went back to Kozarac. I want you to tell us when he went back to Kozarac, for how long he had been at the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Sunday, on 3rd May, when we arrived at our -- at my brother-in-law's, Ljubomir Tadic, we spent Sunday night at his place. Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday we stayed there. Throughout that time we were staying at my brother-in-law's flat while we were cleaning up the other house. I was washing the rugs and Dule was painting the walls, etc. Then on Thursday when we moved into that house, Dule left for Kozarac. He did not stay with us. He just simply helped us move in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be a convenient moment, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: MIRA TADIC, recalled. Examined by MR. KAY, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having moved into this house in Koste Jarica, did you come to know any of the people who lived around you in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us who your neighbours were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Dragoje Balte and his wife and also the grandmother on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you known Mr. Balte before you moved into this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No translation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not get an answer there, your Honour. It is cut out.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think we have a need for another interpreter -- just wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the question, please? We are waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the microphone may have cut out, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How often did you see Mr. Balte?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would see him often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that Dusko Tadic left to go to Kozarac after you had moved into the house. Did he ever visit you back there? Did he ever return from Kozarac for periods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he would visit. He visited us several times. He brought our stuff from the house, the stuff we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the purpose for Dusko Tadic returning to Kozarac after you had moved into this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went back in order to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the coffee bar in Kozarac still open at this time, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to work in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recollect the date when Kozarac was attacked and the conflict in Kozarac started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 24th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that period from when you had moved into the house and until 24th May, how often would you say Dusko had been back to that house in Banja Luka where you were staying with the rest of the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 7th and 23rd May he came on several occasions and on 23rd May, it was a Saturday, he joined us in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time of the day then on 23rd May did he join you in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think between somewhere 5.00 and 6 o'clock in the afternoon, that is, 17 and 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know where he had come from before he had been to see you in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he came from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how he travelled from Prijedor to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarac he went with Trivo Reljic by car. This is our neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did that take him when he went with Trivo Reljic by car from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did he travel from Prijedor to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prijedor to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trivo went to his house in Svodno and my husband went for Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How? Do you know how?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By train.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he have his own vehicle or any other form of transport for himself at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When he arrived then on 23rd May at this place in Koste Jarica, had you and the children and your mother-in-law settled into the house by this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But what was the state of the accommodation like for you as a family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was mostly temporary accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that your husband had returned from Kozarac several times and had brought things from the family home. Did you have much of your own possessions with you there in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 23rd May then when your husband arrived from Prijedor by train, what did you do that evening when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that evening we went to visit our friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What friends are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just set a redaction mark. You saw them that evening. How far away did they live from where you were in Koste Jarica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is on the other side of Banja Luka, some four or five kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you get to that house where you went that evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did you go there to that house to see those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they were our friends and we also wanted to share our feelings about fleeing our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From what you could tell of the mood of your husband when he came to Banja Luka on this evening of 23rd May, what was the state of affairs in Kozarac by that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very tense and desperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the ultimatum that had been given by the Prijedor authorities to the people of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the ultimatum concerning the delivery up of arms by the people within that town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know if by that time of your husband coming on 23rd May whether they had complied with that ultimatum from Prijedor by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you stay at the house of that couple that you had walked to in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed until Sunday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had they been old friends of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you both know them well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry. I have lost track of the days of the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The 24th May is a Saturday, your Honour -- Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the redaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. It will be granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged. [To the witness]: So had you and the family stayed overnight with that couple?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then on next day -- you told us that you left in the afternoon -- where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean on Sunday 24th or on Monday 25th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, you have told us that you arrived at the house of your friends on the evening of 23rd May, which is a Saturday, and that you stayed there until the afternoon of the next day which would be Sunday, 24th May. When you left their house, did you go back to that place in Koste Jarica where you had been staying previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long then did you remain living in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lived there up until 27th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 27th June where did you go to live from that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We moved into a flat in Pecani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I now want to talk to you about that period of time then from 23rd May until 27th June when you are living in Koste Jarica in Banja Luka. During that time did you get a job in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your husband have a job in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he remain living with you in Banja Luka until you moved to Pecani on 27th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he left before us for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect when that was that he left for Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 15th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then in that period from 23rd May until 15th June, was he living with you in Banja Luka or was he living elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With us in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By "living" I mean staying the night and you all being based there as a family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did you and he and the rest of the family spend your time in Banja Luka during this period until 15th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that period we were mostly visiting our friends in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did either of you have much money at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have many friends in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, real friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to Dusko Tadic's brother Ljubo. Was he in Banja Luka as well at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he lived nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any times that your husband Dusko left Banja Luka to travel elsewhere during this period between 23rd May and 15th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know where he travelled to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us then where did he go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went to Kozarac to see the state of our family house, the first time round.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know when that was, when he, as you have said it, the first time round went to Kozarac to look at the state of the family home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was some seven or eight days after the conflict in Kozarac. I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the only time, as far as you know, that he visited Kozarac during this period or were there other times when he visited Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the first time, that was the first time. Then he also went there another time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that other time was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember the date, but it was a couple of days after the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am going to ask you some questions now about that first time when he went to Kozarac. Did he go on his own or with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With his brother Ljubomir Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he away for the day or for any longer period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One day, he was away for one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time did they leave Banja Luka or what time did you last see him on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You recollect the particular time in the morning or is it just a general .....

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how they travelled to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that they went by a car. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that any car owned by your husband or would that have been someone else's vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my husband did not have a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So if they travelled by another car, whose car would that have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. It might have been Ljubo's car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What time did they return from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they came back in the afternoon. I do not know exactly when, but they returned quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did they get back to Banja Luka from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By car most probably. I do not know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you actually see them return to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they came to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they have anything with them when they returned on this first visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you are thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they have anything with them? You said they went to look at the family home -- no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not bring anything on that first occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the second occasion which was a few days later, was your husband away for one day or for a longer period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For two days on the second occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, do you know if he went with anyone or did he travel alone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With his brother Ljubomir Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know when they left Banja Luka on this second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact date. It was a couple of days after that first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But do you know what time of day that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They also left in the morning, and they came back the following day in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how they travelled to Kozarac on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly how they left, but I know that they returned in a lorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whose lorry was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That lorry belonged to a guy from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did they return in a lorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they brought the stuff from our family home, from the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of stuff did they bring from the home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought all the linen from the house and then they also brought the interior part, I mean, the thing that was -- everything that was inside the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, "the interior part"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That means things that are inside the ceiling, like in a form of a net and then parts of the bar, then the glasses and all the things that are needed in a cafe, like, for example, coffee cups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
